newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac, Kohl back Romania, Slovenia for NATO.
newsitem.headline: Chirac, Kohl back Romania, Slovenia for NATO.

text.p: The leaders of France and Germany said on Friday they wanted Romania and Slovenia to be allowed to join NATO from the start of the alliance's enlargement despite U.S. objections.

President Jacques Chirac and Chancellor Helmut Kohl both endorsed the two candidates after the United States said on Thursday it wanted to restrict the first wave of NATO expansion to three central European countries -- the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland.
"We will indeed support the candidacy of Romania despite the reticence expressed by the American government," Chirac told a news conference after a Franco-American summit in Poitiers.

"There is no doubt about the entry of three countries. There is a now discussion about whether three or five countries come into line, including Romania and Slovenia," Kohl said, saying Germany wanted all five to be given a clear message at a NATO summit in Madrid in July that they would be part of the development of the alliance.

Playing down Thursday's White House statement that U.S. President Bill Clinton would only support the entry of the three favourites in the first wave of enlargement, Kohl said: "One individual statement is in no way an advance decision."

A French official said the U.S. position, which went against the wishes of a majority of European NATO allies for a broader enlargement, appeared to be dictated by the higher cost and concern in Congress over the budgetary implications.

France has been in the vanguard of European countries campaigning for Romania and Slovenia to be admitted, arguing that the move would show the alliance's concern for security in the Balkans, the Black Sea area and the Mediterranean.
Germany only came out publicly in favour of Romania and Slovenia at a meeting of European centrist parties this week.
